key_insight: Microscopic residual impurities in wide-bandgap perovskite films act as degradation nucleation sites, and can be rapidly detected with microscopy plus machine learning.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, non-invasive pre-screening of perovskite thin films to improve reliability and scalability for solar-cell manufacturing.
method: Nano-FTIR spectroscopy chemically identified harmful impurities.
High-resolution reflected-light microscopy captured impurity patterns.
Machine-learning image analysis quantified impurity density within seconds.
evidence_signal: Photo-stress experiments showed degradation starts at impurity–perovskite interfaces, and films with higher impurity density degraded faster early on.
watch_item: The imaging workflow should be chemically validated on each film stack and may need recalibration across processing recipes, compositions, and microscope setups.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
